database_summary: Small club/organization schema capturing events, members, finances (budget, income, expense), attendance, member demographics (major, zip). Mix of descriptive entities (member, major, zip_code, event, budget) and transactional/event tables (attendance, income, expense). Keys are opaque text ids. Dates are stored as TEXT. Some columns are low-cardinality enums (positions, event types, budget categories).

accepted.name: member_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  member_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email,
  position,
  t_shirt_size,
  phone,
  zip,
  link_to_major
FROM member
accepted.description: One-row-per-member cleaned projection exposing member attributes and foreign keys for joins. Use when analyses need member demographic fields and FKs to major/zip. Normalizes NULLs for optional fields. | Use for: List members with contact info and demographic attributes; Join members to attendance/income/expense/budget by member_id; Filter members by position, t_shirt_size, or major

accepted.name: event_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  event_name,
  event_date,
  type,
  notes,
  location,
  status
FROM event
accepted.description: One-row-per-event projection exposing event descriptive attributes. Use for event-level filters and joins. Keeps event_date as-is (text) for downstream parsing or filtering. | Use for: Event listings and filters by type, location, or status; Join events to attendance or budget; Convert event_date to date/time formats outside the CTE

accepted.name: attendance_edge
accepted.description: One-row-per-attendance record (event-member link). Use as the base bridge when counting attendees, listing attendees per event, or joining member/event details. | Use for: Count attendees per event; List events attended by a member; Join to member_dim or event_dim for enriched attendance reports

accepted.name: budget_line
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  budget_id,
  category,
  spent,
  remaining,
  amount,
  event_status,
  link_to_event
FROM budget
accepted.description: One-row-per-budget line item with monetary columns exposed. Use for budget rollups, join to event, and to link expenses via link_to_budget. | Use for: Summarize budget spent/remaining by event or category; Link expense rows to budget lines; Filter budget lines by event_status or category

accepted.name: expense_fact
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  expense_id,
  expense_description,
  expense_date,
  cost,
  approved,
  link_to_member,
  link_to_budget
FROM expense
accepted.description: One-row-per-expense transaction exposing date, cost, approval flag, and foreign keys for joins. Keep approved as-text for downstream boolean normalization. | Use for: Total expenses by member, budget, or date range; Filter approved/unapproved expenses; Join to budget_line or member_dim for contextual reporting

accepted.name: income_fact
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  income_id,
  date_received,
  amount,
  source,
  notes,
  link_to_member
FROM income
accepted.description: One-row-per-income record exposing receipt date, amount, source, and member linkage for revenue analyses and member dues tracking. | Use for: Aggregate income by source or date; Member dues history and totals; Join income to member_dim for payer details

accepted.name: member_with_major_zip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.member_id,
  m.first_name,
  m.last_name,
  m.email,
  m.position,
  m.t_shirt_size,
  m.phone,
  m.zip,
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.type AS type,
  z.city AS city,
  z.county AS county,
  z.state AS state,
  z.short_state AS short_state,
  m.link_to_major,
  mj.major_id AS major_id,
  mj.major_name AS major_name,
  mj.department AS department,
  mj.college AS college
FROM member m
LEFT JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code
LEFT JOIN major mj ON m.link_to_major = mj.major_id
accepted.description: Denormalized member row joined to major and zip_code dimensions to expose member demographics and geography in one row. Use when needing member, major, and zip/city/state info together. | Use for: Map members to city/state and major details; Filter members by college/department/city; Prepare member lists for mailing or segmentation

accepted.name: event_attendance_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.event_id,
  e.event_name,
  e.event_date,
  e.type,
  e.location,
  e.status,
  COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count
FROM event e
LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id
GROUP BY
  e.event_id,
  e.event_name,
  e.event_date,
  e.type,
  e.location,
  e.status
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of attendance per event (one row per event) with event descriptive columns preserved. Use for attendance trends, event popularity, and joins to budgets or expenses by event. | Use for: Rank events by attendance; Correlate attendance with event type or location; Detect low-attendance events for follow-up

accepted.name: budget_by_event
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.link_to_event,
  SUM(COALESCE(b.amount,0)) AS total_budget_amount,
  SUM(COALESCE(b.spent,0.0)) AS total_spent,
  SUM(COALESCE(b.remaining,0.0)) AS total_remaining
FROM budget b
GROUP BY b.link_to_event
accepted.description: One-row-per-event summarizing budget totals: budgeted amount, spent, and remaining across budget lines linked to each event. Use for event-level financial summaries and ROI calculations. | Use for: Compare budgeted vs spent by event; Identify events overspent or underspent; Join to event_dim for event metadata

accepted.name: member_financials
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.member_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(i.amount),0) AS total_income_amount,
  COALESCE(SUM(e.cost),0.0) AS total_expense_cost
FROM member m
LEFT JOIN income i ON i.link_to_member = m.member_id
LEFT JOIN expense e ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id
GROUP BY m.member_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-member aggregating total income paid and total expenses charged to the member. Use to compute net contribution by member or identify high-cost members. | Use for: List members by net financial contribution; Find members with high expenses or dues; Prepare member billing or reimbursement summaries

accepted.name: latest_expense_per_budget
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  expense_id,
  expense_description,
  expense_date,
  cost,
  approved,
  link_to_member,
  link_to_budget
FROM (
  SELECT
    expense_id,
    expense_description,
    expense_date,
    cost,
    approved,
    link_to_member,
    link_to_budget,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY link_to_budget ORDER BY expense_date DESC, expense_id) AS rn
  FROM expense
) sub
WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: Latest expense row per link_to_budget based on expense_date text ordering. Use when you need the most recent expense for each budget line. Keeps full expense row for joins. | Use for: Get the most recent expense for each budget line; Compare latest expense dates across budgets; Use as deduplicated sample when budgets expect one recent transaction

accepted.name: event_financials
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.event_id,
  e.event_name,
  e.event_date,
  e.type,
  e.location,
  e.status,
  COALESCE(bagg.total_budget_amount,0) AS total_budget_amount,
  COALESCE(bagg.total_spent,0.0) AS total_spent,
  COALESCE(bagg.total_remaining,0.0) AS total_remaining,
  COALESCE(att.attendee_count,0) AS attendee_count
FROM event e
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    link_to_event,
    SUM(COALESCE(amount,0)) AS total_budget_amount,
    SUM(COALESCE(spent,0.0)) AS total_spent,
    SUM(COALESCE(remaining,0.0)) AS total_remaining
  FROM budget
  GROUP BY link_to_event
) bagg ON bagg.link_to_event = e.event_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    a.link_to_event,
    COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count
  FROM attendance a
  GROUP BY a.link_to_event
) att ON att.link_to_event = e.event_id
accepted.description: Event-level join combining event metadata, aggregated budget totals, and attendee count in one row. Use for dashboards comparing attendance and finances per event. | Use for: Assess event ROI (attendance vs spend); Identify events with high spend and low attendance; Create event summary reports for stakeholders
